$comment: Mtek CPU numeric conformance table (spec/testing.md section 5; format: decision 0037).
Each case: id (unique), fn (Mtek callee: intrinsic, namespace function, vector constructor, conversion
target type, binary operator, 'neg' for unary minus, or a comparison), args and expect as typed values,
portable (false: NaN, infinities, f32 division by zero and other cases the GPU need not reproduce), note.
Typed values: {"f32": x}, {"i32": n}, {"u32": n}, {"bool": b}, {"vec2"|"vec3"|"vec4"|"quat"|"color": [..]},
{"mat4": [16 column-major]}. Every f32 is a JSON number that is exactly a binary32 value, or one of the
strings "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity", "-0". Expected values are the specified CPU results, bit for bit
(NaN: any NaN). Validated by crates/mtek-compiler/tests/numeric_cpu_table.rs (independent Rust oracle;
MTEK_BLESS=1 rewrites expect and the canonical layout) and by packages/runtime-web/src/math/conformance.test.ts.
